<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
<meta name="description" content="Python Programming — From Installation to Your First Program">
<title>Python Programming — From Installation to Your First Program</title>

<style>
/* =========================================================
   RBUtech Python Learning Page 1
   Unique CSS Prefix: py1-
   ========================================================= */

.py1-page,
.py1-page * {
    box-sizing: border-box;
}

.py1-page {
    --py1-bg: #f5f7fb;
    --py1-panel: #ffffff;
    --py1-panel-soft: #f8fafc;
    --py1-text: #172033;
    --py1-muted: #64748b;
    --py1-line: #e2e8f0;
    --py1-primary: #4f46e5;
    --py1-primary-dark: #3730a3;
    --py1-secondary: #06b6d4;
    --py1-success: #059669;
    --py1-warning: #d97706;
    --py1-danger: #dc2626;
    --py1-purple: #7c3aed;
    --py1-pink: #db2777;
    --py1-code: #111827;
    --py1-code-text: #e5e7eb;
    --py1-radius: 18px;
    --py1-shadow: 0 12px 35px rgba(15,23,42,.08);

    width: 100%;
    min-height: 100vh;
    background:
        radial-gradient(circle at 10% 0%, rgba(79,70,229,.08), transparent 28rem),
        radial-gradient(circle at 90% 10%, rgba(6,182,212,.07), transparent 26rem),
        var(--py1-bg);
    color: var(--py1-text);
    font-family:
        Inter,
        ui-sans-serif,
        system-ui,
        -apple-system,
        BlinkMacSystemFont,
        "Segoe UI",
        sans-serif;
    line-height: 1.65;
}

.py1-container {
    width: min(1180px, calc(100% - 32px));
    margin: auto;
}

.py1-hero {
    position: relative;
    overflow: hidden;
    padding: 64px 0 46px;
    background:
        linear-gradient(135deg, #111827 0%, #1e1b4b 48%, #312e81 100%);
    color: #fff;
}

.py1-hero::before,
.py1-hero::after {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    border-radius: 50%;
    filter: blur(2px);
    opacity: .18;
}

.py1-hero::before {
    width: 320px;
    height: 320px;
    background: #22d3ee;
    top: -150px;
    right: 5%;
}

.py1-hero::after {
    width: 260px;
    height: 260px;
    background: #a78bfa;
    bottom: -160px;
    left: 5%;
}

.py1-hero-inner {
    position: relative;
    z-index: 2;
}

.py1-badge {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 8px;
    padding: 7px 13px;
    border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);
    border-radius: 999px;
    background: rgba(255,255,255,.08);
    font-size: 13px;
    font-weight: 700;
    letter-spacing: .04em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
}

.py1-python-mark {
    width: 38px;
    height: 38px;
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    border-radius: 11px;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg,#3776ab,#ffd343);
    font-weight: 900;
    color: white;
}

.py1-hero h1 {
    max-width: 850px;
    margin: 22px 0 14px;
    font-size: clamp(34px, 5vw, 62px);
    line-height: 1.06;
    letter-spacing: -.045em;
}

.py1-hero p {
    max-width: 800px;
    color: #cbd5e1;
    font-size: clamp(16px, 2vw, 20px);
}

.py1-hero-meta {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: 10px;
    margin-top: 26px;
}

.py1-meta-chip {
    padding: 8px 13px;
    border-radius: 10px;
    background: rgba(255,255,255,.09);
    border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.12);
    color: #e2e8f0;
    font-size: 14px;
}

.py1-progress-wrap {
    margin-top: 34px;
    max-width: 700px;
}

.py1-progress-top {
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
    gap: 15px;
    margin-bottom: 8px;
    font-size: 13px;
    color: #cbd5e1;
}

.py1-progress {
    height: 10px;
    border-radius: 999px;
    overflow: hidden;
    background: rgba(255,255,255,.12);
}

.py1-progress-bar {
    width: 20%;
    height: 100%;
    border-radius: inherit;
    background: linear-gradient(90deg,#22d3ee,#818cf8);
    transition: width .35s ease;
}

/* General sections */

.py1-section {
    padding: 58px 0;
}

.py1-section-alt {
    background: rgba(255,255,255,.62);
    border-top: 1px solid rgba(226,232,240,.7);
    border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(226,232,240,.7);
}

.py1-section-heading {
    margin-bottom: 28px;
}

.py1-eyebrow {
    display: inline-block;
    margin-bottom: 8px;
    color: var(--py1-primary);
    font-size: 12px;
    font-weight: 800;
    letter-spacing: .1em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
}

.py1-section-heading h2 {
    margin: 0 0 8px;
    font-size: clamp(27px, 4vw, 40px);
    line-height: 1.15;
    letter-spacing: -.035em;
}

.py1-section-heading p {
    max-width: 760px;
    margin: 0;
    color: var(--py1-muted);
}

/* Cards */

.py1-grid {
    display: grid;
    gap: 18px;
}

.py1-grid-2 {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr));
}

.py1-grid-3 {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr));
}

.py1-card {
    background: var(--py1-panel);
    border: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
    border-radius: var(--py1-radius);
    padding: 23px;
    box-shadow: var(--py1-shadow);
}

.py1-card h3 {
    margin: 0 0 8px;
    font-size: 19px;
}

.py1-card p {
    color: var(--py1-muted);
}

.py1-icon-card {
    position: relative;
    overflow: hidden;
}

.py1-icon-card::after {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    width: 90px;
    height: 90px;
    border-radius: 50%;
    background: rgba(79,70,229,.06);
    right: -25px;
    bottom: -30px;
}

.py1-icon {
    width: 44px;
    height: 44px;
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    border-radius: 13px;
    margin-bottom: 13px;
    color: white;
    font-weight: 900;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg,#4f46e5,#06b6d4);
}

/* Objectives */

.py1-objectives {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr));
    gap: 12px;
}

.py1-objective {
    display: flex;
    gap: 12px;
    align-items: flex-start;
    padding: 15px;
    background: #fff;
    border: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
    border-radius: 14px;
}

.py1-check {
    flex: 0 0 auto;
    width: 25px;
    height: 25px;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    border-radius: 50%;
    background: #ecfdf5;
    color: var(--py1-success);
    font-weight: 900;
}

/* Mind map */

.py1-mindmap {
    position: relative;
    min-height: 610px;
    overflow: hidden;
    padding: 30px;
    border-radius: 24px;
    border: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
    background:
        radial-gradient(circle at center,rgba(79,70,229,.08),transparent 25%),
        #fff;
    box-shadow: var(--py1-shadow);
}

.py1-mindmap-center {
    position: absolute;
    z-index: 3;
    left: 50%;
    top: 50%;
    transform: translate(-50%,-50%);
    width: 190px;
    min-height: 90px;
    padding: 18px;
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    justify-content: center;
    text-align: center;
    border-radius: 22px;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg,#4f46e5,#7c3aed);
    color: white;
    box-shadow: 0 18px 45px rgba(79,70,229,.28);
    font-weight: 900;
}

.py1-mindmap-center small {
    margin-top: 4px;
    color: #ddd6fe;
    font-weight: 600;
}

.py1-mind-node {
    position: absolute;
    z-index: 3;
    width: 145px;
    padding: 13px 10px;
    text-align: center;
    border-radius: 14px;
    border: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
    background: white;
    box-shadow: 0 8px 22px rgba(15,23,42,.08);
    font-weight: 800;
    font-size: 14px;
}

.py1-node-line {
    position: absolute;
    z-index: 1;
    height: 2px;
    transform-origin: left center;
    background: linear-gradient(90deg,#a5b4fc,#cbd5e1);
}

.py1-node-1 { left: 5%; top: 11%; }
.py1-node-2 { left: 41%; top: 5%; }
.py1-node-3 { right: 5%; top: 12%; }
.py1-node-4 { left: 3%; top: 45%; }
.py1-node-5 { right: 3%; top: 45%; }
.py1-node-6 { left: 8%; bottom: 9%; }
.py1-node-7 { left: 41%; bottom: 4%; }
.py1-node-8 { right: 8%; bottom: 9%; }
.py1-node-9 { right: 2%; bottom: 39%; }

.py1-node-line.l1 { width: 245px; left: 48%; top: 48%; transform: rotate(-140deg); }
.py1-node-line.l2 { width: 205px; left: 50%; top: 48%; transform: rotate(-105deg); }
.py1-node-line.l3 { width: 250px; left: 52%; top: 48%; transform: rotate(-42deg); }
.py1-node-line.l4 { width: 205px; left: 48%; top: 50%; transform: rotate(174deg); }
.py1-node-line.l5 { width: 205px; left: 52%; top: 50%; transform: rotate(6deg); }
.py1-node-line.l6 { width: 220px; left: 47%; top: 53%; transform: rotate(137deg); }
.py1-node-line.l7 { width: 190px; left: 50%; top: 53%; transform: rotate(78deg); }
.py1-node-line.l8 { width: 220px; left: 53%; top: 53%; transform: rotate(43deg); }
.py1-node-line.l9 { width: 205px; left: 52%; top: 50%; transform: rotate(-3deg); }

/* Teaching pattern */

.py1-concept-box {
    margin-top: 25px;
    padding: 22px;
    border-radius: 16px;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg,#f8fafc,#eef2ff);
    border: 1px solid #e0e7ff;
}

.py1-concept-box strong {
    color: var(--py1-primary-dark);
}

.py1-real {
    margin-top: 13px;
    padding: 13px 15px;
    border-left: 4px solid var(--py1-secondary);
    border-radius: 8px;
    background: #ecfeff;
}

.py1-mistake {
    margin-top: 13px;
    padding: 13px 15px;
    border-left: 4px solid var(--py1-warning);
    border-radius: 8px;
    background: #fffbeb;
}

.py1-practice {
    margin-top: 13px;
    padding: 13px 15px;
    border-left: 4px solid var(--py1-purple);
    border-radius: 8px;
    background: #f5f3ff;
}

/* Flow diagrams */

.py1-flow {
    display: flex;
    align-items: stretch;
    justify-content: center;
    gap: 0;
    margin: 25px 0;
    overflow-x: auto;
    padding: 12px 5px 25px;
}

.py1-flow-step {
    position: relative;
    flex: 0 0 145px;
    min-height: 125px;
    padding: 17px 12px;
    text-align: center;
    border: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
    border-radius: 16px;
    background: white;
    box-shadow: 0 8px 22px rgba(15,23,42,.07);
}

.py1-flow-step strong {
    display: block;
    margin-bottom: 7px;
    color: var(--py1-primary-dark);
}

.py1-flow-step span {
    display: block;
    color: var(--py1-muted);
    font-size: 12px;
}

.py1-flow-arrow {
    flex: 0 0 45px;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    color: var(--py1-primary);
    font-size: 25px;
    font-weight: 900;
}

/* Installation */

.py1-install-step {
    display: flex;
    gap: 16px;
    padding: 18px 0;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
}

.py1-install-step:last-child {
    border-bottom: 0;
}

.py1-step-number {
    flex: 0 0 38px;
    height: 38px;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    border-radius: 11px;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg,#4f46e5,#06b6d4);
    color: white;
    font-weight: 900;
}

.py1-install-step h3 {
    margin: 0 0 5px;
}

.py1-install-step p {
    margin: 0;
    color: var(--py1-muted);
}

.py1-terminal {
    margin-top: 18px;
    padding: 18px;
    overflow-x: auto;
    border-radius: 14px;
    background: #0b1220;
    color: #d1fae5;
    font-family: "Cascadia Code","Consolas",monospace;
    font-size: 14px;
}

/* Code */

.py1-code-card {
    margin: 20px 0;
    overflow: hidden;
    border: 1px solid #1f2937;
    border-radius: 16px;
    background: var(--py1-code);
    box-shadow: 0 12px 30px rgba(15,23,42,.12);
}

.py1-code-header {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: space-between;
    gap: 10px;
    padding: 10px 14px;
    background: #1f2937;
    color: #cbd5e1;
    font-size: 12px;
    font-weight: 700;
}

.py1-copy {
    border: 1px solid #475569;
    border-radius: 7px;
    padding: 5px 9px;
    background: #334155;
    color: white;
    cursor: pointer;
    font-size: 11px;
}

.py1-copy:hover {
    background: #475569;
}

.py1-code-card pre {
    margin: 0;
    padding: 20px;
    overflow-x: auto;
    color: var(--py1-code-text);
    font-family: "Cascadia Code","Fira Code","Consolas",monospace;
    font-size: 14px;
    line-height: 1.7;
}

.py1-k { color: #c084fc; }
.py1-s { color: #86efac; }
.py1-f { color: #67e8f9; }
.py1-n { color: #fbbf24; }
.py1-c { color: #94a3b8; }

/* Output */

.py1-output {
    margin: -10px 0 20px;
    padding: 14px 17px;
    border-radius: 10px;
    background: #ecfdf5;
    border: 1px solid #bbf7d0;
    color: #166534;
    font-family: monospace;
}

.py1-output strong {
    font-family: inherit;
}

/* Tables */

.py1-table-wrap {
    overflow-x: auto;
    margin: 20px 0;
}

.py1-table {
    width: 100%;
    border-collapse: collapse;
    background: white;
    border-radius: 14px;
    overflow: hidden;
    border: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
}

.py1-table th,
.py1-table td {
    padding: 12px 14px;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
    text-align: left;
}

.py1-table th {
    background: #f1f5f9;
    color: #334155;
}

.py1-table code {
    padding: 3px 6px;
    border-radius: 5px;
    background: #eef2ff;
    color: #3730a3;
}

/* Variable diagram */

.py1-memory {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 1fr 70px 1fr;
    gap: 15px;
    align-items: center;
    margin: 25px 0;
}

.py1-memory-names,
.py1-memory-values {
    display: grid;
    gap: 12px;
}

.py1-memory-item {
    padding: 14px;
    border-radius: 13px;
    border: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
    background: white;
    box-shadow: 0 5px 15px rgba(15,23,42,.05);
}

.py1-memory-name {
    color: var(--py1-primary-dark);
    font-family: monospace;
    font-weight: 800;
}

.py1-memory-value {
    color: #047857;
    font-family: monospace;
    font-weight: 800;
}

.py1-memory-arrow {
    display: grid;
    gap: 31px;
    text-align: center;
    color: var(--py1-primary);
    font-size: 25px;
}

/* Data types */

.py1-type-tree {
    display: grid;
    gap: 15px;
    margin-top: 25px;
}

.py1-type-root {
    margin: auto;
    padding: 15px 24px;
    border-radius: 14px;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg,#4f46e5,#7c3aed);
    color: white;
    font-weight: 900;
}

.py1-type-branches {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(3,1fr);
    gap: 12px;
}

.py1-type {
    padding: 16px;
    border-radius: 14px;
    border: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
    background: white;
}

.py1-type code {
    display: inline-block;
    margin-bottom: 5px;
    padding: 4px 8px;
    border-radius: 7px;
    background: #eef2ff;
    color: var(--py1-primary-dark);
    font-weight: 800;
}

.py1-type small {
    display: block;
    color: var(--py1-muted);
}

/* Operators */

.py1-operator-card {
    border-top: 4px solid var(--py1-primary);
}

.py1-operator-list {
    display: grid;
    gap: 7px;
    margin-top: 15px;
}

.py1-operator-item {
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
    gap: 12px;
    padding: 9px 11px;
    border-radius: 8px;
    background: #f8fafc;
}

.py1-operator-item code {
    color: var(--py1-primary-dark);
    font-weight: 800;
}

/* Error cards */

.py1-error {
    border-left: 4px solid var(--py1-danger);
}

.py1-error h3 {
    color: #b91c1c;
}

.py1-error code {
    color: #b91c1c;
}

/* Interactive */

.py1-interactive {
    padding: 24px;
    border-radius: 18px;
    border: 1px solid #c7d2fe;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg,#eef2ff,#ecfeff);
}

.py1-button {
    border: 0;
    border-radius: 10px;
    padding: 10px 15px;
    background: var(--py1-primary);
    color: white;
    font-weight: 800;
    cursor: pointer;
    transition: transform .15s ease, background .15s ease;
}

.py1-button:hover {
    background: var(--py1-primary-dark);
    transform: translateY(-1px);
}

.py1-button.secondary {
    background: #334155;
}

.py1-answer {
    display: none;
    margin-top: 13px;
    padding: 14px;
    border-radius: 10px;
    background: #ecfdf5;
    border: 1px solid #a7f3d0;
    color: #065f46;
}

.py1-answer.show {
    display: block;
}

/* Quiz */

.py1-quiz-question {
    margin-bottom: 25px;
    padding: 20px;
    border: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
    border-radius: 15px;
    background: white;
}

.py1-quiz-question h3 {
    margin-top: 0;
}

.py1-option {
    display: block;
    margin: 8px 0;
    padding: 11px 13px;
    border-radius: 9px;
    background: #f8fafc;
    border: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
    cursor: pointer;
}

.py1-option:hover {
    background: #eef2ff;
}

.py1-option input {
    margin-right: 8px;
}

.py1-feedback {
    margin-top: 10px;
    font-weight: 800;
}

.py1-correct {
    color: var(--py1-success);
}

.py1-wrong {
    color: var(--py1-danger);
}

/* Checklist */

.py1-checklist {
    display: grid;
    gap: 10px;
}

.py1-check-row {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 12px;
    padding: 13px;
    border: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
    border-radius: 11px;
    background: white;
}

.py1-check-row input {
    width: 18px;
    height: 18px;
    accent-color: var(--py1-primary);
}

.py1-completion {
    display: none;
    margin-top: 18px;
    padding: 17px;
    border-radius: 13px;
    background: #ecfdf5;
    border: 1px solid #86efac;
    color: #166534;
    font-weight: 700;
}

.py1-completion.show {
    display: block;
}

/* Summary */

.py1-summary {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(3,1fr);
    gap: 15px;
}

.py1-summary-item {
    padding: 18px;
    border-radius: 15px;
    background: white;
    border: 1px solid var(--py1-line);
}

.py1-summary-item strong {
    display: block;
    margin-bottom: 6px;
    color: var(--py1-primary-dark);
}

/* Navigation */

.py1-navigation {
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
    gap: 18px;
    align-items: center;
    padding: 28px;
    border-radius: 22px;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg,#111827,#312e81);
    color: white;
}

.py1-navigation p {
    margin: 5px 0 0;
    color: #cbd5e1;
}

.py1-next {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 8px;
    padding: 12px 18px;
    border-radius: 11px;
    background: white;
    color: #312e81;
    font-weight: 900;
    text-decoration: none;
}

.py1-footer {
    padding: 35px 0;
    text-align: center;
    color: var(--py1-muted);
    font-size: 13px;
}

/* Responsive */

@media (max-width: 850px) {
    .py1-grid-3,
    .py1-summary {
        grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
    }

    .py1-type-branches {
        grid-template-columns: repeat(2,1fr);
    }

    .py1-mindmap {

            setTimeout(function () {

        } catch (error) {

                    score + "/" + total +
                    " (" + percentage + "%). Review the missed concepts.";

                    "You scored " +
                    score + "/" + total +

        var completed = 0;

        checklist.forEach(function (item) {

            if (item.checked) {
                completed++;
            }

        });

        var percent =
            Math.round(
                (completed / checklist.length) * 100
            );

        if (progressBar) {

            /*
             * Page 1 represents 20% of the five-page course.
             * Checklist completion moves the page progress from
             * 20% toward 40%.

            var courseProgress =
                20 + (percent * 0.2);

            progressBar.style.width =

        }

        if (completion) {

            if (completed === checklist.length) {
                completion.classList.add("show");
            } else {
                completion.classList.remove("show");
            }
        }

        try {

            var state = {};

pages.body:
Python Programming • Page 3 of 5

Functions, Classes and Object-Oriented Programming

Move from writing individual Python statements to designing reusable, maintainable programs with functions, classes, inheritance, polymorphism and composition.

Learning progress 0%

Complete the checklist as you learn.

Page contents
Introduction Mind Map Functions Parameters & Arguments Return Values Scope Lambda & Functional Tools Classes & Objects Constructors Encapsulation Inheritance Polymorphism Composition Student Project Exercises Quiz Summary

1. Introduction

In the previous lessons you learned how Python stores data, makes decisions, and repeats operations. Now we will learn how to organize larger programs.

Functions Reusable blocks of behavior that can accept input and produce output.
Classes Blueprints for creating objects that combine data and behavior.
Objects Individual instances created from classes.
OOP A programming style that models software around objects and relationships.

Learning objectives

2. Functions and OOP Mind Map

The central idea is reusable Python code. Functions reuse behavior; classes reuse structure and behavior.

Diagram A — Reusable Python Code
Functions
Parameters
Return Values
Scope
Lambda
REUSABLE
PYTHON CODE
Classes
Objects
Encapsulation
Inheritance
Polymorphism
Composition

3. Functions

Why functions are needed

A function is a named, reusable block of code that performs a specific task.

Why it matters: Without functions, the same calculation or operation may be copied throughout your program. Functions give you one place to maintain the logic.
Real-world analogy: Think of a coffee machine. You press a button instead of manually performing every step required to make coffee.
calculator.py 
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

result = add(10, 20)
print(result)
30

The def keyword defines the function. The function receives a and b, calculates their sum, and returns the result.

Common mistake: Defining a function does not execute it. You must call it: add(10, 20).
Exercise: Create a subtract(a, b) function that returns the difference.

Function execution flow

Diagram B — Function Execution Flow
Function call: add(10, 20)
↓
Arguments passed: 10 and 20
↓
Function body executes
↓
Return value produced: 30
↓
Caller receives result

Calculator functions

calculator.py 
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

def subtract(a, b):
    return a - b

def multiply(a, b):
    return a * b

def divide(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        return "Cannot divide by zero"
    return a / b

print(add(10, 5))
print(subtract(10, 5))
print(multiply(10, 5))
print(divide(10, 5))
15 5 50 2.0

4. Parameters and Arguments

Parameters describe what a function accepts. Arguments are the actual values you provide when calling the function.

Diagram C — Parameters versus Arguments
Definition 
def greet(name, message="Hello"):
    return f"{message}, {name}!"
name → parameter
message → parameter with a default value
↓
greet("Asha", "Welcome")
"Asha" → positional argument
"Welcome" → positional argument

Positional arguments

Values are assigned according to their position.

positional.py 
def introduce(name, age):
    print(name, age)

introduce("Asha", 21)
Asha 21

Keyword arguments

Keyword arguments explicitly identify the parameter being assigned.

keyword.py 
def introduce(name, age):
    print(name, age)

introduce(age=21, name="Asha")
Asha 21

Default arguments

default.py 
def greet(name, message="Hello"):
    return f"{message}, {name}"

print(greet("Asha"))
print(greet("Ravi", "Welcome"))
Hello, Asha Welcome, Ravi
Analogy: A default argument is like a form field with a pre-filled value. You can accept the default or provide a different value.

*args

Use *args when a function should accept any number of positional arguments.

args.py 
def total(*args):
    return sum(args)

print(total(10, 20))
print(total(1, 2, 3, 4, 5))
30 15

**kwargs

Use **kwargs when a function should accept any number of keyword arguments.

kwargs.py 
def show_profile(**kwargs):
    for key, value in kwargs.items():
        print(key, "=", value)

show_profile(
    name="Asha",
    age=21,
    course="Python"
)
name = Asha age = 21 course = Python
Common mistake: Do not confuse *args with a list. Inside the function, args is a tuple.
Exercise: Create a function called average(*numbers) that returns the average of all supplied numbers.

5. Return Values

The return statement sends a value back to the code that called the function.

multiple_values.py 
def calculate(a, b):
    total = a + b
    difference = a - b
    product = a * b

    return total, difference, product

result = calculate(20, 5)

print(result)
print(result[0])
print(result[1])
print(result[2])
(25, 15, 100) 25 15 100

Python can return multiple values. Technically, Python packages them into a tuple.

Analogy: A restaurant can return an entire meal containing several items instead of returning only one item.
Exercise: Create a function that receives a student's marks and returns: total, average, and highest mark.

6. Variable Scope

Scope determines where a variable can be accessed.

Diagram D — Local and Global Scope
GLOBAL SCOPE
school = "RBUtech"
FUNCTION SCOPE

def student():

name = "Asha"

age = 20

name and age are local variables. They exist inside the function.

scope.py 
school = "RBUtech"

def show_student():
    name = "Asha"

    print(school)
    print(name)

show_student()

print(school)
RBUtech Asha RBUtech
Common mistake: Trying to access a local variable outside the function causes a NameError.
Analogy: A global variable is like a notice board visible to everyone in a building. A local variable is like a private note inside one office.
Exercise: Create a global variable tax_rate and a function with a local variable price. Calculate the final price.

7. Lambda and Functional Tools

Lambda functions

A lambda is a small anonymous function. It is useful when a short function is needed only once or as an argument to another function.

lambda.py 
square = lambda x: x * x

print(square(5))
25

map()

map() applies a function to every item in an iterable.

map.py 
numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

squares = list(map(lambda x: x * x, numbers))

print(squares)
[1, 4, 9, 16, 25]

filter()

filter() keeps items for which a function returns True.

filter.py 
numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]

even_numbers = list(
    filter(lambda x: x % 2 == 0, numbers)
)

print(even_numbers)
[2, 4, 6]
Use lambda when: The operation is tiny and simple.
Use map when: Every item needs to be transformed.
Use filter when: You need to select matching items.
Prefer normal def when: The logic is complex or reused.
Exercise: Use filter() to keep only students whose marks are at least 50.

8. Classes and Objects

A class is a blueprint. An object is a concrete instance created from that blueprint.

Diagram E — Class and Object Relationship
Student
Attributes
  • name
  • age
  • marks
Methods
  • introduce()
  • calculate_grade()
→
student1
Asha
Age: 20
Marks: 90

student2
Ravi
Age: 21
Marks: 75

student3
Sara
Age: 19
Marks: 88
Why it matters: A class lets you model real-world entities while keeping their data and behavior together.
Analogy: A class is an architectural blueprint. Each house built from the blueprint is an object.
student.py 
class Student:

    def introduce(self):
        print("I am a Python student.")

student1 = Student()
student2 = Student()

student1.introduce()
student2.introduce()
I am a Python student. I am a Python student.

Instance attributes and methods

student_attributes.py 
class Student:

    def introduce(self):
        print(f"My name is {self.name}")

student = Student()

student.name = "Asha"

student.introduce()
My name is Asha

Instance attributes belong to individual objects. Instance methods operate on those objects and normally receive self.

Exercise: Create a Book class with title, author, and a describe() method.

9. Constructors

Python commonly uses __init__() to initialize an object when it is created.

Diagram F — Constructor Execution
Student("Asha", 90)
↓
__init__() runs
↓
self.name = "Asha"
↓
self.mark = 90
↓
Initialized object
constructor.py 
class Student:

    def __init__(self, name, mark):
        self.name = name
        self.mark = mark

    def show(self):
        print(self.name, self.mark)

student = Student("Asha", 90)

student.show()
Asha 90
Common mistake: The constructor is named exactly __init__ with two underscores on each side.
Exercise: Create a Product class whose constructor accepts name and price.

10. Class Attributes, Class Methods and Static Methods

Class attributes

A class attribute is shared by objects of the class.

class_attribute.py 
class Student:

    school = "RBUtech"

    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

a = Student("Asha")
b = Student("Ravi")

print(a.school)
print(b.school)
RBUtech RBUtech

Class methods

A class method receives the class itself as cls.

classmethod.py 
class Student:

    school = "RBUtech"

    @classmethod
    def school_name(cls):
        return cls.school

print(Student.school_name())
RBUtech

Static methods

A static method does not require either an instance or class reference. It is useful for helper logic related conceptually to the class.

staticmethod.py 
class Student:

    @staticmethod
    def is_valid_mark(mark):
        return 0 <= mark <= 100

print(Student.is_valid_mark(90))
print(Student.is_valid_mark(120))
True False
Feature Receives Use when
Instance method self Working with an object's data
Class method cls Working with class-level state or alternate constructors
Static method Nothing automatically Utility logic related to the class

11. Encapsulation

Encapsulation means controlling how an object's internal state is accessed or changed.

Diagram H — Encapsulation
Application
↓
Public method: deposit()
↓
Object validation
↓
Internal state update
Analogy: An ATM does not let you directly modify the bank's database. You interact through controlled operations such as deposit and withdrawal.
bank_account.py 
class BankAccount:

    def __init__(self, balance=0):
        self._balance = balance

    def deposit(self, amount):
        if amount <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Amount must be positive")

        self._balance += amount

    def withdraw(self, amount):
        if amount > self._balance:
            raise ValueError("Insufficient funds")

        self._balance -= amount

    def get_balance(self):
        return self._balance


account = BankAccount(100)

account.deposit(50)
account.withdraw(30)

print(account.get_balance())
120
Important: Python does not enforce private fields in the same way as some languages. A leading underscore is primarily a convention meaning "internal use".
Exercise: Add a withdraw() validation rule that rejects negative or zero withdrawal amounts.

12. Inheritance

Inheritance allows a child class to reuse behavior from a parent class.

Diagram G — Inheritance
Person
↓
Student
Employee
inheritance.py 
class Person:

    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

    def introduce(self):
        print(f"My name is {self.name}")


class Employee(Person):

    def work(self):

Complete runnable program

student_management.py 
class Student:

    def __init__(self, name, marks):
        self.name = name
        self.marks = marks

    def average(self):
        if not self.marks:
            return 0

        return sum(self.marks) / len(self.marks)

    def grade(self):
        avg = self.average()

        if avg >= 90:
            return "A"
        elif avg >= 80:
            return "B"
        elif avg >= 70:
            return "C"
        elif avg >= 60:
            return "D"
        else:
            return "F"

    def display(self):
        print("\nStudent:", self.name)
        print("Marks:", self.marks)
        print("Average:", round(self.average(), 2))
        print("Grade:", self.grade())


def read_mark(subject):
    while True:
        try:
            mark = float(
                input(f"Enter marks for {subject}: ")
            )

            if 0 <= mark <= 100:
                return mark

            print("Marks must be between 0 and 100.")

        except ValueError:
            print("Please enter a valid number.")


students = []

while True:

    print("\n--- Student Management ---")
    print("1. Add student")
    print("2. Display students")
    print("3. Exit")

    choice = input("Choose an option: ")

    if choice == "1":

        name = input("Enter student name: ")

        subjects = ["Python", "Math", "English"]
        marks = []

        for subject in subjects:
            marks.append(read_mark(subject))

        student = Student(name, marks)
        students.append(student)

        print("Student added successfully.")

    elif choice == "2":

        if not students:
            print("No students available.")
        else:
            for student in students:
                student.display()

    elif choice == "3":

        print("Goodbye!")
        break

    else:
        print("Invalid choice.")

Functions Package reusable behavior into named blocks.

When should you use each concept?

Concept Use it when...
Function You have reusable behavior or a task that deserves a name.
Parameters The behavior needs input.
Return The caller needs a result.
*args The number of positional inputs can vary.
**kwargs The number of named inputs can vary.
Lambda A tiny one-expression function is sufficient.
Class Data and behavior naturally belong together.
Inheritance There is a genuine "is-a" relationship and useful shared behavior.
Encapsulation State needs controlled access or validation.
Polymorphism Different objects should support the same operation.
Composition A larger object is built from smaller cooperating objects.
Architect's rule: Do not use classes simply because Python supports classes. Start with simple functions and data structures. Introduce classes when your program contains objects with meaningful state, behavior, and relationships.
